request.report:
Round 4 (spec-replay) analysis of off-greedy, A-greedy, B-greedy complete; bench/m1-notes.md fixed.

Findings (results/2026-10-12/m1-ngram/replay/{off,A,B}-greedy/requests.jsonl + server logs):
- Spec is ACTIVE in A and B (draft-acceptance lines in all 4 phases incl. 2-slot dual) with --mmproj loaded -> mmproj does NOT block text-only speculation. Corrected §3: the only spec refusal is `unsupported batch.has_embd + spec case` (server-context.cpp:3550-3553) for batches carrying embeddings; text-only (this replay) is fine. No refusal hit, no -nommproj fallback needed.
- fg decode tok/s (greedy, sum predicted_n/sum predicted_ms): single-agent off 55.1 / A 86.0 / B 53.4; single-mem 55.6/53.1/50.7; dual-agent 26.3/25.5/23.0; dual-mem 25.0/23.8/22.4.
- A single-agent 86.0 is inflated by 3 spec-induced length-finishes (loops): r1/2/8 (1323), mem0-r0/0/2 (3121), mem0-r2/0/2 (4854); off finished the two mem ones normally with tool_calls (1020/3701). No-length A single-agent = 54.3 < off 55.1 -> a quality regression, not a speedup.
- Combined two-slot throughput (dual): off 52.5 / A 52.6 (flat) / B 49.0 (agent); dual-mem 51.5/49.2/46.6. Neither A nor B beats off with both slots busy.
- temp-0 output identity NOT preserved: spec changes greedy even with draft_n=0 (baseline-r0/0/0: off 530c… vs A cdad…, both 71 tok).

Prod arm choice: A (higher dual-agent greedy, 25.5 > B 23.0; also wins dual-mem and no-length).

Next: prod sampling (temp 1.0 agent / 0.2 mem) for off, then A. Then final decision (default = do NOT deploy, since no gain with both slots busy) + serving experiment page + series/project summaries.
